newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's Beanie Babies gobbled up, supplies run low.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's Beanie Babies gobbled up, supplies run low.

text.p: A sign on the McDonald's restaurant door said it all: "Sorry. We are out of Teenie Beanie Babies."

McDonald's Corp., launching what may be its most successful Happy Meals promotion, hoped to give away 100 million miniature versions of the popular Ty Inc. Beanie Babies toys over five weeks, beginning April 11.
But the Beanie Boom was so huge, supplies are dwindling across the country, and the McDonald's promotion will end far sooner than expected.
"I don't think supplies will go that long," said Jack Greenberg, chairman of McDonald's USA division.
There are a few pockets of Teenie Beanies across the country, although some areas have already run out, added McDonald's spokeswoman Anna Rozenich.
From day one, Beanies meant big business for McDonald's, which is the largest fast-food chain with more 21,000 units worldwide.
"I've almost tripled my Happy Meal sales in my restaurants," said Lindsay Hughes, a franchisee with two McDonald's restaurants in Los Angeles.
In southern California, there are still Teenie Beanies to be found. "I have plenty," added Hughes, who is vice chairman of McDonald's Operators National Advertising Fund.
At the Park Ridge, Ill., McDonald's Thursday evening, three preschoolers played with their Teenie Beanies -- two blue spotted lizards and a yellow duck -- the last of that restaurant's supplies.
"What time did you get here?" one woman asked from her table where her two children looked over their alternative loot. Hearing the reply, she sighed, "We got here 10 minutes too late."

As with every craze, there are stories of extravagance and excess, like the person who supposedly bought 300 Happy Meals but took food for only 50, or the person who bought 20 Happy Meals, took out the toys, and tossed the food away.

The popularity of the Teenie Beanies reflects the run-away success of the full-sized Beanie Babies as toys and collector's items. An Internet Web Site entitled "Kim's Beanie Babies" averages 6 million hits a week and lists auctions for Beanies.
"We captured this toy's popularity," McDonald's Rozenich said. "It's an incredible phenomenon."

Collectors, it seemed, went to great lengths to try to get each of the 10 Teenie Beanies offered by McDonald's by buying multiple meals at different stores. While some McDonald's did allow customers to choose the Beanies they wanted, the dwindling supplies did limit the choices.

"I was at a McDonald's in Rosemont (Illinois) and there were four lines, about 25 people deep," said Art, a 35-year-old Indiana resident. "The manager came out and said, 'we only have seals.' People groaned."
